about.title: Title Loan Calculator - Vehicle Title Cash Advance Cost & APR Estimator
about.description: The Title Loan Calculator estimates monthly payment, total fees, and effective APR for short-term loans secured by your vehicle title. Compare payoff scenarios, understand rollover impact, and evaluate alternatives to avoid high-cost borrowing and potential repossession risk.

howTo.title: How to Use the Title Loan Calculator

steps.title: Enter Loan Amount
steps.description: Input the amount you plan to borrow based on your car's title value.

steps.title: Add Fees & Term
steps.description: Include interest/fees and select the short repayment term (often 30 days).

steps.title: Model Rollovers
steps.description: If you can't repay on time, add rollovers to see cost escalation.

steps.title: Review Payment & APR
steps.description: See total repayment, effective APR, and the portion going to fees.

steps.title: Compare Alternatives
steps.description: Test secured/unsecured personal loans or credit union options for lower cost.

tips: Borrow the minimum needed and avoid rollovers to limit fees.
Understand repossession risk—default may result in losing your vehicle.
Check for state caps and consumer protections in your area.

features.title: Effective APR
features.description: Annualizes fees and short terms to show the true borrowing cost.

features.title: Rollover Impact
features.description: Estimates how renewals quickly increase total repayment.

features.title: Payment Breakdown
features.description: Visualize principal vs. fees/interest across the term.

features.title: Collateral Considerations
features.description: Highlights how vehicle value and state rules influence pricing and risk.

faq.a: A short-term loan secured by your vehicle title, typically with high fees and risk of repossession if you default.
Yes. Rollovers add fees and drastically raise the effective APR and total repayment.
Consider credit union small-dollar loans, personal installment loans, or negotiating payment plans with creditors.
If you default on a title loan, the lender may repossess the vehicle to recover losses—review your contract carefully.
